description:
On develop f822f0f84, def id(f), do: f called with fn x -> x + 1 end and with &String.upcase/1 fails to compile: 'call to +/2 violates its @spec for arguments (binary, int)'. Elixir prints both results. The same happens for def wrap(f), do: {:w, f} and for a recursive wrap_after(f, n) that returns {:w, f} at n = 0.

Mechanism (measured):
- A caller reads its callee's return by key alone: prepare_function_call (jobs/semantic.rs) reads world.activation_return(&activation), which is one return joined over every evidence row under that key.
- A non-recursive key erases a closure's brand wherever demand.local is Ignore (derive_activation_key_arrow, types/mod.rs). It does not consult demand.returned, so a callable the body returns but never tests loses its identity. Both lambdas reach one key, the published return is the union of both, and each caller applies both lambdas.
- A recursive key keeps a returned position as its addressed convergence class (convergence_collapse_returned -> convergence_class_at), and that class turns a pure callable into an address var. Same blend.
- type-specialization.md and addressed-arrow.md state this as design ('brands still erase' at a returned position). It contradicts the rule both docs give: an activation's published return may depend only on what its key names.

Not affected (probed, pass on develop): a callable returned inside a new closure's captures, a callable chosen by a literal the body tests, a callable read out of a list pattern.

Experiment D (local switch, never committed): skip brand erasure at a returned slot, and keep a returned pure callable verbatim (literals widened) in convergence_class_at. Results:
- every probe above prints Elixir's answer on interp and run;
- distiller (tools/distill-telemetry.exs over main_returns_one.jsonl, interp): 12,892 -> 12,892 jobs, identical output;
- 00420: 2,513 -> 2,637 jobs, all in Enum.reduce_while/3 (9 -> 25 executables): each Enum wrapper's reducer lambda now keys its own activation, because the return is built from what that reducer returns. That is the rule's cost, paid where develop joined the returns of every reducer under one key.

Full suite under D (FZ_EXP_D=1, develop f822f0f84): every fixture passes except 00632 on all three paths ('backend type test cannot read lane-form ShapeId(..)'). That is a pre-existing defect D exposes, not one it makes: u4 (pick(flag, fn x -> x + 1 end, 5) with ONE caller, then a clause chosen by integer-or-closure) fails the same way on develop. 00632 passes on develop only because its three callers blend three lambdas into one return, and a join of distinct callable producers is marked escaped (runtime_demand.rs, delivered_join_has_distinct_callable_producers), which boxes it. One lambda joined with an integer is not marked, and transport gives the union an exact direct-callable layout (layout_from_demand -> exact_direct_callable_layout) that has no room for the integer. Gating the exact layout on a pure-callable type gets past the type test and then fails at the apply seam (no construction wrapper published), so the fix belongs in the runtime-demand fact that decides boxing, not at layout.

Pins under D: 00420 census 2,513 -> 2,637 and its activation/executable-fact pins; 00571 executables 188 -> 199, Activation claims 191 -> 202, body walks 508 -> 530; same-shape lambda chain 33 -> 34; callable owner metadata 180 -> 212; aggregate 1,325 -> 1,379. Where the rise comes from (measured with a local print of InputDemand): Enum.reduce_while/3's returned axis is [Ignore, Whole, Whole]. No body in its cone returns the reducer (every local return mask is Ignore at the reducer); the Whole is stated by keying.rs visit_protocol_callback, which marks every non-receiver input of a protocol callback as returned because an implementation may hand an accumulator back. So the reducer of every Enum wrapper keys per lambda. The rule is right to keep a returned callable; the claim that this callable is returned is the conservative part.

Acceptance:
- fixture 01153_a_returned_callable_keeps_its_identity (id, wrap, recursive wrap_after; oracle) passes on interp, run and build;
- one rule in code: a position the returned axis keeps keeps callable identity on both key paths;
- type-specialization.md and addressed-arrow.md state the rule (a returned callable keeps its brand), with the old 'brands still erase' text removed;
- pin moves attributed per pin, rises authorized before commit.
title: A callable a function returns keeps its identity in the function's key, so two callers never share one return
